p: I sing to my: The prophet by this song sets before the people's eyes their ingratitude and God's mercy.
wellbeloved a song of my beloved: That is, to God.
vineyard in a very fruitful hill: Meaning that he had planted his Church in a place most plentiful and abundant.
and built a tower in the: He spared no diligence or cost.
wild grapes: In Isa 5:7 he declares what they were.
between me and my vineyard: He makes them judges in their own cause, for as much as it was evident that they were the cause of their own ruin.
will take away its hedge: I will take no more care for it: meaning, that he would take from them his word and ministers and all other comforts, and feed them contrary plagues.
judgment: Judgment and righteousness are true fruit of the fear of God and therefore in the cruel oppression there is no religion.
a cry: Of them who are oppressed.
place: That is, for the poor to dwell in.
ears said the LORD of hosts: I have heard the complaint and cry of the poor.
bath: Which contains about 5 gallons, so that every acre would yield only half a gallon.
homer shall yield an: Which contains 50 gallons.
ephah: An ephah contains 5 gallons and is in dry things as much as a bath is in liquids.
rise early in the morning: Who spare no pain nor diligence to follow their lusts.
night: Who are never weary of their rioting and excessive pleasures but use all means to provoke to the same.
work of the LORD: They do not regard the provident care of God over them, nor for what end he has created them.
have gone into captivity: That is, will certainly go: for so the prophets use to speak as though the thing which will come to pass were done already.
no knowledge: Because they would not obey the word of God.
hell hath enlarged herself: Meaning, the grave will swallow up them who will die for hunger and thirst, and yet for all this great destruction it will never be satisfied.

the lambs feed after their manner: God comforts the poor lambs of his Church, who had been strangers in other countries, promising that they would dwell in these places again, of which they had been deprived by the fat and cruel tyrants.
cords of vanity: Who use all allurements, opportunities and excuses to harden their conscience in sin.
Let him make speed: He shows what are the words of the wicked, when they are menaced by God's judgments, 2Pe 3:4.
and good evil: Who are not ashamed of sin, nor care for honesty but are grown to a desperate impiety.
wise in their own eyes: Who contemn all doctrine and admonition.
mighty to drink wine: Who are never weary, but show their strength, and brag in gluttony and drunkenness.
root shall be as rottenness: Both they and their posterity so that nothing will be left.

hand against them: He shows that God had so sore punished this people, that the dumb creatures if they had been so plagued would have been more sensible, and therefore his plagues must continue, till they begin to seal them.
to the nations from afar: He will make the Babylonians come against them at his beck, and to fight under his standard.
be weary nor stumble among them: They will be prompt and lusty to execute God's vengeance.
the latchet of their shoes be: The enemy will have no impediment.
roar: By which is declared the cruelty of the enemy.
one looketh to the land: The Jews will find no comfort.
heavens: In the land of Judah.
